slides.h: A galaxy was measured, and the design became permanent
b: 2,840 galaxies now carry a real chirality value. The day before, that number was 0.
From the first one, the study's own rules forbid changing any parameter — the run is void if we do, not merely embarrassing.

slides.h: The achievement was 2 days of deliberately not measuring
b: 2 parameters were still choosable. Choosing them one day later would have voided the run instead of delaying it.
A preregistration is worth something only because the choices are made before the data can influence them.
The first real measurement is where that protection either holds or quietly fails.

slides.h: Rehearse on fake galaxies to see what is still undecided
b: It found 2 live parameters: the allocator refuses when a prior reaches 0 or 1, so a smoothing rule had to exist.
And 30 galaxies per stratum was satisfiable in rehearsal only because a synthetic sample can be engineered and a real one cannot.

slides.h: The document freezing those choices cited the wrong file
b: Its engineering claim quoted a line from a different revision of the harness than its evidence came from.
Its byte-for-byte check pointed at a file a later run had overwritten.
An adversarial review caught both. Held, repaired, re-gated before anything was measured — which is the reason to trust the rest of this.

slides.h: Every value carries the hashes of everything that made it
b: The raw float bits sit beside the decimal, so a number cannot drift in transcription or be reproduced by a different instrument without it showing.

slides.h: No average, no tertile, no summary until the last galaxy
b: Looking at any aggregate now would let the data influence the strata that decide which galaxies get hand-checked.
Transfer finishes around Tuesday; measurement follows minutes behind; strata form once, on the complete sample.
If a stratum comes up short the frozen answer is to hold and declare it underpowered — not to improvise.
